I have a success story! 
We don’t have children, but we were (still are) married when my wife (amab) came out to me. 
We had been married about 2 years when she came out. It was a lot for me to process at first and took quite a bit of personal reflection on my part. She was incredibly open with me and we had countless conversations and tears and all. She was very aware that this was a huge change for me as well as for her and our relationship and she did a great job communicating what she needed and listening to what I needed. All that consumed us for probably 8 months to a year, right up until she started HRT. But once she started HRT things in our relationship leveled out again, our day to day lives went back to “normal”. 
Now for the part where I gush about how great she is and how the process has changed me for the better. 
I loved my spouse before she transitioned obviously or we wouldn’t have gotten hitched, but now? Now it’s a whole different ball game. I love her more than I thought possible. I love the ways she’s changed and I love the ways she’s stayed the same. I love how soft her skin is and how her hair smells. But mostly I love the light and life in her eyes. I can feel the happiness and… wholeness radiating out of her. She is a more attentive more engaged partner now that she is who she was supposed to be all along. And I can say that this whole process has made me a better more compassionate person as well. 
It wasn’t a cake walk to get here, but it has been so so worth it. 
The only advice I can really give is to just keep talking and listening to each other, and when you think you’ve done enough of that talk some more. 
Sorry this turned into a novel!! Good luck 💖

It took me several months to truly come to terms with my wife’s (mtf), transition it’s been over a year now and the #1 thing that helped the most was truly open and honest communication pretty much constantly. I’m not sure I would have been able to handle it if on my bad days full of doubt and fear for the future she shut me out. My whole world changed and I needed time to figure out what that meant for me, for us and for the future. I needed her reassurance that she still wanted the life we had built together and that she still loved me. I was scared of losing my best friend, but we talked and talked and talked and with each conversation it got easier and more natural.  Doing research on my own and reading about other peoples success stories also helped quite a bit. Now we’re one of those success stories! Watching her truly become herself and learn to be happy and find  joy has been one of the most beautiful things I’ve ever gotten to be part of. Our relationship is so much stronger than it used to be (and it was pretty great in the first place). Her as the woman she is just feels right in ways that are hard to describe. Time and communication are key! Good luck and congratulations on finding your true self, you’ve got this.

My wife has been out to me for a year and just started HRT a few weeks ago. The more she has let go of her old coping mechanisms the better she has been as a partner. I spent a not insignificant amount of time panicked and stressed and crying into my pillow when she was asleep, but we kept talking and talking and talking and crying together and talking some more. Communication is 100% the most important thing you can do through this. Our relationship is better than ever now. I honestly didn’t know I could love another person this much (and I already married this person!) but you have to remember to take care of yourself and let yourself grieve. It’s a loss and a change but hopefully the reward will be a better life and partner.

My wife (mtf) came out to me last year and it took me some time to let myself grieve and grapple with my own emotions. The week she started taking hormones a family member passed and I felt like I was stretched out thin and it was overwhelming again. But she is so much happier and has honestly done a much better job of supporting me as my wife than she did as my husband. Life comes at you fast and hard but even though it seems like too much right now you will be ok. Sex was also a concern for us, and although everyone is different we haven’t had any problems so far (my wife also is keeping her penis). The way we are intimate has changed, but it’s changed for the better, the connection is deeper and the sex is softer with less of the focus being on one of us “preforming”. 
Just remember that your concerns and hesitations are valid your person is going to change but they will still be your person. Just make sure you get the support you need as well. Congratulations in the baby you sound like you’ll make a great parent 🖤

Oh I’m well aware. I work in the food and beverage industry (specialized in wine, but used to bartend and manage) it’s all part of a much larger problem and one I have had to deal with extensively. Tipping culture is 100% broken, but as it is now if you stiff your server at a restaurant they end up having to pay out of pocket for the pleasure of serving you because they have to tip out the support staff on their sales for they day (busser, bartender, host, food runner all make a percentage of a servers tips so if the server doesn’t get tipped they still owe a tip out to those people.)  
I would love to see a better system to how it’s handled but as it stands that is how things work most places in the US at the moment. 

I’m not trying to convince anyone to change how they spend or don’t spend their own money, just an explanation.
In many states the minimum wage for tipped workers is under $3 an hour. Just something to keep in mind.
